questions.question: What is energy and what is its unit? Give three examples of energy changing from one form to another.
questions.expected_answer: Energy is what is needed to make things happen: to make things work, move, live, heat up, light up or make sound. It is measured in joules (J); 1 kilojoule = 1 000 J. Examples: a gas stove changes chemical energy into heat and light; a torch changes chemical energy in the battery into electrical energy and then light; a person changes chemical energy from food into kinetic energy and heat; a solar panel changes light into electrical energy.

questions.question: Explain the difference between renewable and non-renewable energy sources and give two examples of each.
questions.expected_answer: Non-renewable sources cannot be replaced within a human lifetime because they form far more slowly than they are used, so they will run out; examples coal, crude oil, natural gas, uranium (nuclear fuel). Renewable sources are replaced naturally as fast as they are used, so they will not run out; examples sunlight (solar), wind, hydro (flowing water), biofuel (wood, biogas).

questions.question: Give two advantages and two disadvantages of coal as a source of electricity in South Africa, and two advantages and one disadvantage of solar energy.
questions.expected_answer: Coal advantages: concentrated energy source; available day and night in any weather; large reserves in South Africa and existing power stations. Coal disadvantages: non-renewable, will run out; burning releases carbon dioxide causing climate change; air pollution harms health; mining damages land and water. Solar advantages: renewable; no carbon dioxide or air pollution when generating; South Africa has very strong sunshine; can be used on individual roofs. Solar disadvantage: does not work at night and is reduced by clouds, so needs batteries or backup; panels and storage cost money to install.
